From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Hosting residency + air-gap constraints — post-call recap (Sage Health)

Hi Emma / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with corrections or missing items.

Summary of pain / goals
- Data residency: PHI must remain in US-only regions; certain datasets must be restricted to a single-state region for regulatory reasons.
- Air-gap requirement: For model training and certain inferencing traces, your security team wants an air-gapped option (no outbound internet from inference nodes).
- No public IPs: Preferred deployment without public IPs on worker nodes; access via customer VPN / transit gateway only.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS / HSM required; we need an integration plan for key rotation and access auditing.
- Third-party restrictions: No unmanaged connectors to external analytics vendors; only allow outbound to approved monitoring endpoints via controlled proxy.
- Audit & retention: Audit logs retained for 7 years; access to immutable audit records is required for compliance review.

Immediate goals
1) Produce a short checklist mapping Redwood options to your constraints (Private VPC in your cloud / on-prem air-gapped bundle / dedicated reserved capacity in your VPC).
2) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with your infra/security teams to validate network topology and HSM integration assumptions.
3) Agree on timeline and initial scope for a proof-of-concept (POC) — minimal dataset + 2-week observation window.

Notes / assumptions from our side
- We can run Redwood Private in a customer VPC (no public egress from nodes) or deliver an on-prem packaged bundle for fully air-gapped environments.
- HSM integration requires coordination with your security team and physical or cloud KMS details; estimate 2–3 week lead time after network access is established.
- Some observability features (agent-based metrics export) will need an approved egress path; we can work with a push model to an internal metrics endpoint rather than pulling from your network.

Attachments: SageHealth-Residency-Notes.pdf, Redwood-VPC-Checklist.xlsx (first pass mapping)

Next steps (please confirm)
- Emma / Tom: share preferred windows for the technical deep dive (targeting Wed 6/9 or Thu 6/10).
- Provide a high-level network diagram (VPC/subnets/firewalls) and the contact for your network engineer.
- Confirm whether HSM will be cloud-managed (AWS KMS/CloudHSM) or a vendor appliance on-prem.

If you’re OK I’ll create a HubSpot activity and share a draft SOW outline for initial POC sizing and timing.

Thanks,

Neha Kapoor

Neha — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our security team after the call: 

- Confirmed: PHI and derived artifacts need to be stored in-region (US) and for some studies remain within a single-state boundary (we’ll share which states are in scope).
- Air-gap: We do need an option where inference hosts have no internet egress. Instrumentation can be forwarded to an internal collector only.
- HSM: We are planning to use AWS CloudHSM for first phase, but long-term we may evaluate a FIPS-certified appliance on-prem.
- Audit retention: 7 years for logs; we will provide retention policy docs. We also want to ensure log signing / immutability where possible.
- Network: Ashburn (us-east-1) VPC for initial POC; we’ll send a redacted network diagram.

We can do the deep dive Wed 6/9 at 1:00 PM ET / 10:00 AM PT. Tom will coordinate providing the network diagram and the infra contact (Kunal).

On the procurement side: if Redwood can provide a draft SOW and a high-level estimate for a 6-week POC (license + infra run costs), procurement will be ready to review once we have the tech confirmation.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Director, Infrastructure Security | Sage Health
emma@sagehealth.com

Quick technical notes ahead of tomorrow’s call: 

- Static routing & IP allowlist: We’ll need a/b test of the required IP ranges for the POC. Ideally we get a static prefix or a transit gateway peer so your firewall rules are stable.
- No outbound: For fully air-gapped nodes, we’ll run a push-only telemetry exporter to your internal collector (TLS to private endpoint). We cannot rely on third-party SaaS endpoints.
- HSM integration: CloudHSM is straightforward; if you plan a physical HSM we’ll need certs and a network plan for appliance connectivity. Lead time 2–3 weeks for integration and testing.
- Data residency enforcement: We support per-tenant isolation; please identify which datasets must be single-state-restricted so we can lock placement/policy in the deployment manifest.
- E2E encryption: We can enable endpoint-to-disk encryption and customer-controlled keys; we’ll need KMS access roles to be provisioned for a service principal during POC.

Please send the redacted network diagram and the contact for Kunal (your network engineer). I’ll bring a short checklist of the technical artifacts we need at the start of the POC.

Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
